name: 德米特里·肖斯塔科维奇

points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 肖斯塔科维奇出生于圣彼得堡的一个知识分子家庭，父亲是工程师，母亲是音乐教师。他从小就展现出非凡的音乐天赋，9岁时开始跟随母亲学习钢琴。1919年，13岁的肖斯塔科维奇考入列宁格勒音乐学院，成为该校历史上最年轻的学生之一。这段时期的音乐教育为他后来的创作奠定了坚实基础，同时也培养了他对古典音乐的深刻理解和独特见解。
points.descriptionEn: Shostakovich was born in Saint Petersburg into an intellectual family with his father as an engineer and mother as a music teacher. He displayed exceptional musical talent from a young age, beginning piano lessons with his mother at age 9. In 1919, at just 13, he entered the Leningrad Conservatory, becoming one of its youngest students in history. This period of musical education laid the foundation for his later compositions and cultivated his deep understanding and unique perspective on classical music.

points.title: 求学与早期创作
points.description: 在列宁格勒音乐学院，肖斯塔科维奇师从著名钢琴家尼古拉·马尔科和作曲家马克西利安·施泰因贝格。1923年，他开始在钢琴班学习，1926年转入作曲班。1926年，他创作的第一交响曲在列宁格勒首演，获得巨大成功，引起国际乐坛关注。这一时期他还创作了《第一钢琴奏鸣曲》、《第二交响曲》等作品，逐渐形成了自己的音乐风格。1927年，他在华沙国际钢琴比赛中获得荣誉奖，进一步确立了他在音乐界的地位。
points.descriptionEn: At the Leningrad Conservatory, Shostakovich studied under renowned pianist Nikolai Malko and composer Maximilian Steinberg. He began in the piano class in 1923, then switched to composition in 1926. His First Symphony, premiered in Leningrad in 1926, was a tremendous success, gaining international attention. During this period, he also composed works like the First Piano Sonata and Second Symphony, gradually developing his unique musical style. In 1927, he received an honorary award at the International Chopin Piano Competition in Warsaw, further establishing his position in the music world.

points.title: 艺术争议与成熟
points.description: 1933年，肖斯塔科维奇移居莫斯科，艺术创作进入新阶段。1934年，他的歌剧《姆钦斯克的麦克白夫人》在列宁格勒首演后获得巨大成功，但随后遭到官方批判。1936年，斯大林在《真理报》上发表文章谴责这部歌剧为'形式主义'，这成为苏联文化政策转向的标志性事件。面对政治压力，肖斯塔科维奇不得不修改自己的创作风格。1937年，他创作了《第五交响曲》，这部作品表面上是向政治妥协，但内含深刻的社会批判，成为他最受欢迎的作品之一。这一时期他还创作了《第六交响曲》、《钢琴五重奏》等重要作品。
points.descriptionEn: In 1933, Shostakovich moved to Moscow, entering a new phase of his artistic career. His opera Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District, premiered in Leningrad in 1934, was initially a great success but later faced official criticism. In 1936, Stalin published an article in Pravda condemning the opera as 'formalism,' marking a turning point in Soviet cultural policy. Facing political pressure, Shostakovich had to modify his compositional style. In 1937, he composed his Fifth Symphony, which appeared to be a political compromise but contained deep social criticism, becoming one of his most popular works. During this period, he also created important works like the Sixth Symphony and Piano Quintet.

points.title: 战争岁月
points.description: 二战期间，肖斯塔科维奇留在被围困的列宁格勒，亲身经历了战争的残酷。1941年，他在被围困的城市中完成了著名的《第七交响曲》（列宁格勒交响曲），这部作品描绘了法西斯侵略的暴行，成为反法西斯斗争的音乐象征。1942年，肖斯塔科维奇和家人才被疏散到莫斯科，后又搬到古比雪夫。1943年，他回到莫斯科，完成了《第八交响曲》。战争期间，肖斯塔科维奇还创作了《第二钢琴奏鸣曲》、《第二弦乐四重奏》等作品，展现了在极端困难条件下坚持创作的精神。他的音乐成为战时苏联人民精神力量的重要象征。
points.descriptionEn: During World War II, Shostakovich remained in the besieged city of Leningrad, personally experiencing the brutality of war. In 1941, while trapped in the city, he completed his famous Seventh Symphony (the 'Leningrad Symphony'), which depicted the atrocities of fascist aggression and became a musical symbol of the anti-fascist struggle. In 1942, Shostakovich and his family were evacuated to Moscow, then later moved to Kuibyshev. In 1943, he returned to Moscow and completed his Eighth Symphony. During the war, he also composed works like the Second Piano Sonata and Second String Quartet, demonstrating his spirit of creative perseverance under extreme conditions. His music became an important symbol of spiritual strength for the Soviet people during wartime.

points.title: 政治压力与创作转型
points.description: 1948年，肖斯塔科维奇再次受到官方批判，被指责为'形式主义'作曲家，与普罗科菲耶夫、哈恰图良等作曲家一起受到谴责。他被禁止公开演出，部分作品被禁演。这一时期，他转向创作更符合官方要求的音乐，包括电影配乐和爱国主义题材作品。然而，他也在这一时期创作了《第十交响曲》、《第一小提琴协奏曲》等深刻作品，以及开始创作弦乐四重奏系列。1953年斯大林去世后，政治环境有所缓和，肖斯塔科维奇的创作获得更多自由。1957年，他完成了《第十一交响曲》（1905年），这部作品反映了俄国革命的历史，获得广泛认可。
points.descriptionEn: In 1948, Shostakovich faced official criticism again, accused of being a 'formalist' composer along with Prokofiev and Khachaturian. He was banned from public performances, and some of his works were prohibited. During this period, he turned to composing music that better aligned with official requirements, including film scores and patriotic works. However, he also created profound works like the Tenth Symphony and First Violin Concerto, and began his string quartet series. After Stalin's death in 1953, the political environment eased, and Shostakovich gained more creative freedom. In 1957, he completed his Eleventh Symphony ('1905'), which reflected Russian revolutionary history and received widespread recognition.

points.title: 晚年成就与遗产
points.description: 1960年代，肖斯塔科维奇的创作进入成熟期，完成了《第十三交响曲》（巴比·雅尔）等具有深刻社会批判意义的作品。1962年，他加入苏联共产党，这一决定引起争议，有人认为这是政治妥协，也有人认为这是他保护自己艺术创作的策略。晚年，肖斯塔科维奇专注于弦乐四重奏创作，共创作了15部四重奏，这些作品被视为他最深刻、最个人化的创作。1975年，肖斯塔科维奇在莫斯科逝世，享年68岁。他的音乐遗产包括15部交响曲、15部弦乐四重奏、6部协奏曲以及大量室内乐、电影配乐和声乐作品，对20世纪音乐产生了深远影响。他的作品既体现了苏联时代的政治压力，又保持了艺术独立性和深刻的人道主义关怀。
points.descriptionEn: In the 1960s, Shostakovich's composition entered a mature phase, completing works with profound social criticism like the Thirteenth Symphony ('Babi Yar'). In 1962, he joined the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, a decision that sparked controversy—some saw it as political compromise, others as a strategy to protect his artistic creativity. In his later years, Shostakovich focused on string quartet composition, creating 15 quartets considered his most profound and personal works. Shostakovich died in Moscow in 1975 at age 68. His musical legacy includes 15 symphonies, 15 string quartets, 6 concertos, and numerous chamber works, film scores, and vocal compositions, exerting profound influence on 20th-century music. His works reflect both the political pressures of the Soviet era and maintain artistic independence and profound humanistic concern.

supporter.zh: 肖斯塔科维奇被视为20世纪最伟大的作曲家之一，他的音乐作品深刻而富有表现力，展现了人类在极端政治环境下的精神韧性。支持者认为，他在苏联严苛的政治环境下，巧妙地在官方要求与个人艺术表达之间找到了平衡，通过隐晦的象征和复杂的音乐语言表达了对自由的渴望和对极权主义的批判。他的15部交响曲和15部弦乐四重奏构成了音乐史上最伟大的创作成就之一，为后人留下了宝贵的音乐遗产。
supporter.en: Shostakovich is regarded as one of the greatest composers of the 20th century, whose music is profound and expressive, demonstrating human spiritual resilience under extreme political conditions. Supporters argue that he skillfully balanced official demands with personal artistic expression in the harsh Soviet political environment, subtly conveying his longing for freedom and criticism of totalitarianism through symbolic references and complex musical language. His 15 symphonies and 15 string quartets constitute one of the greatest creative achievements in musical history, leaving an invaluable legacy for future generations.

critic.zh: 批评者指出，肖斯塔科维奇在政治压力下多次妥协，包括在1948年受到批判后调整创作风格，以及1962年加入苏联共产党等行为。他们认为这些妥协损害了艺术家应有的独立性和 integrity。此外，有学者质疑某些作品如《第十一交响曲》是否真正表达了个人信念，还是仅仅迎合了官方意识形态。批评者还认为，肖斯塔科维奇在自传中的叙述有时存在矛盾和自我美化，难以完全作为研究其生平的可靠依据。
critic.en: Critics point out that Shostakovich compromised multiple times under political pressure, including adjusting his compositional style after the 1948 criticism and joining the Communist Party in 1962. They argue that these compromises undermined the independence and integrity expected of an artist. Additionally, scholars question whether certain works like the Eleventh Symphony truly expressed personal beliefs or merely catered to official ideology. Critics also note that Shostakovich's autobiographical writings contain contradictions and self-aggrandizement, making them unreliable as sole sources for studying his life.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，肖斯塔科维奇被定义为一位在极权主义环境下挣扎的复杂艺术家。他的音乐作品既反映了苏联的政治现实，又超越了时代限制，成为人类普遍情感和思想的表达。他的生平被视为艺术家与政治权力关系的典型案例，展现了在专制制度下如何保持艺术尊严的艰难抉择。肖斯塔科维奇的音乐在全球范围内广泛演出和录制，他的形象既是一位伟大的作曲家，也是一个时代的见证者，其作品继续影响着当代音乐创作和表演。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Shostakovich is defined as a complex artist who struggled under totalitarian conditions. His music both reflects the political reality of the Soviet Union and transcends temporal limitations, becoming an expression of universal human emotions and thoughts. His life is regarded as a typical case study of the relationship between artists and political power, demonstrating the difficult choices involved in maintaining artistic dignity under authoritarian rule. Shostakovich's music is widely performed and recorded worldwide, and his image is both that of a great composer and a witness to his era, with his works continuing to influence contemporary musical composition and performance.

self.zh: 艺术不能是暴力的，艺术应该是人道的。
self.en: Art cannot be violent, art must be humane.

others.zh: 肖斯塔科维奇的音乐是20世纪最伟大的悲剧性作品，它们不仅记录了一个时代的苦难，更超越了时代，成为全人类共同的精神财富。
others.en: Shostakovich's music represents the greatest tragic works of the 20th century; they not only record the suffering of an era but transcend it to become a common spiritual treasure for all humanity.
